A deep dive into Google Trends data reveals a remarkable look at human curiosity, relief, national pride, and some familiar Indian internet habits. On September 30, 2026, Flydubai Flight FZ1073 from Dubai to Tel Aviv faced a sudden mid-air nightmare. The co-pilot stabbed Captain Smit Machchhar inside the cockpit and forced the plane into a terrifying 14,000-foot plunge in under 30 seconds. However, because modern cockpit doors are heavily reinforced, the cabin crew had no way to force their way in from the outside. Despite bleeding heavily from severe stab wounds, Machchhar managed to unlock the door from within. That single move allowed the crew and passengers to rush in and overpower the attacker. Machchhar then regained control and safely made an emergency landing in Tabuk, Saudi Arabia, saving around 180 lives. Praise quickly poured in from world leaders, including Prime Minister Narendra Modi, US President Donald Trump, and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. items.text: Death row killer Christa Pike made final request before surviving botched execution
items.article: Death row killer Christa Pike made a final request before her execution in Tennessee - she survived the procedure despite two lethal injections Christa Pike, the death row inmate who survived two lethal injections this week, made an unusual final request prior to the botched execution. Pike , 50, was administered with two lethal injections in Tennessee’s death chamber but somehow survived. She was rushed to hospital shortly after and remains in a critical condition. She would have been the first woman the state put to death in 200 years. Her attorneys revealed yesterday that the convicted murderer requested no men be involved in administering the lethal drug. She made the request due to her history of suffering sexual abuse, fearing being put to death by a man would be needlessly traumatic. “That was her biggest fear as the victim of sexual abuse, that she would be pinned down, prodded, poked, cut,” one of her lawyers, Stephen Ferrell, said. “What I saw was consistent with that,” another of her lawyers, Randy Spivey, said in response to a question about whether the execution team had been staffed entirely by women. The botched injection saw Pike pinned down for around an hour as staff tried to set the two IV lines that would administer the lethal chemicals and supposedly end her life.

items.key: ai:the gandhi photograph you carry in your wallet: who actually took it and how did it end up on indian currency notes?
items.text: The Gandhi Photograph You Carry In Your Wallet: Who Actually Took It And How Did It End Up On Indian Currency Notes?
items.article: This Gandhi Jayanti, look closely at your Rs 500 note. The famous face on your currency note wasn’t drawn Every day, over a billion people handle Indian currency notes featuring the smiling portrait of Mahatma Gandhi. Yet, despite its presence in almost every wallet across the nation, few know the origins of this iconic image. Contrary to common belief, the portrait is neither an artistic drawing nor an official state portrait. It is a cropped, mirrored section of an authentic photograph taken during a pivotal political meeting in Delhi in 1946. The original photograph was captured outside Viceregal House, now known as Rashtrapati Bhavan, in Delhi. Mahatma Gandhi was attending crucial political negotiations regarding the transfer of power alongside British diplomat Lord Frederick William Pethick-Lawrence. In the original full-length frame, Gandhi is seen standing next to Lord Pethick-Lawrence, sharing a candid, warm smile. The identity of the photographer remains disputed among historical archivists, though many attribute the historic shot to an unknown press photographer working for the British colonial administration. When the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) selected the image for currency design, security designers executed a subtle transformation. Designers cropped Lord Pethick-Lawrence out of the frame entirely, isolating Gandhi’s face and shoulders. items.key: ai:mysuru dasara 2026: the story of nishane aane, the elephant that leads jamboo savari
items.text: Mysuru Dasara 2026: The Story Of Nishane Aane, The Elephant That Leads Jamboo Savari
items.article: Carrying the royal insignia, the Nishane elephant proceeds to a designated point and receives a ceremonial salute. When the grand Jamboo Savari procession winds its way through the streets of Mysuru, thousands of spectators eagerly await one iconic sight: the elephant carrying the glittering golden howdah, or Ambari. It is the defining image of Mysuru Dasara, captured in photographs and celebrated year after year. But before the Ambari elephant makes its appearance, another elephant has already taken the lead. Carrying a flag bearing the royal insignia , it walks at the head of the procession, surrounded by drum beats, musical performances, cultural troupes and cheering crowds. This is the ‘Nishane Aane’, the ceremonial leader of the Jamboo Savari . The term ‘Nishane’ refers to a sign or signal marking the beginning of an event or procession. In the Jamboo Savari, the flag-bearing elephant plays this ceremonial role, announcing the commencement of the grand procession. Carrying the royal insignia, the Nishane elephant proceeds to a designated point and receives a ceremonial salute. This marks the formal beginning of the Jamboo Savari, one of the central attractions of Mysuru Dasara . The Nishane elephant is, therefore, more than just the first elephant in the procession. It holds a distinct ceremonial responsibility, signalling the start of a tradition that draws large crowds to Mysuru every year.
